t: Check if a String Is an Acronym of Words — First Letters
o: Build the string of first characters of words and compare with s. For ["alice","bob","charlie"] the initials form "abc", matching s. For ["an","apple"] the initials are "aa", not "a", so the answer is false. Length must match too, which the string comparison handles automatically.
k: Concatenate words[i][0] for all i and compare to s.
String equality also enforces the length constraint.

a.i: Map each word to its first character, join, and test equality with s. One line in most languages.
s: Extract the first character of every word.
a.t: O(total characters of words) — we touch only the first character of each word plus the comparison.
a.sp: O(number of words) for the built acronym.

w: Trivial; the only subtle failure is comparing lengths separately when building character-by-character with early exit — the join-and-compare version avoids that entirely. Follow-up: check whether s is a subsequence-acronym (each letter from a distinct word in order).
